Kayla Washington

gap-019 · supplement · fictional age 16

Written life first, then interpreted by a separate response author without the engine or results. These are synthetic checks. There is no correct career answer key.

Life from age 4 to 16

I ask questions because I actually want to know, not because I already decided to do that for work. My mom hears one thing about biology and starts talking about degrees. Sometimes I like making a video more than doing anything for school. Then somebody comments and I hate the whole app. I can tell a friend not to compare herself and still do it myself five minutes later.

  • family: Lives with her mother and younger sister; father lives in Louisiana and calls most weeks; mother and daughter have ongoing disagreements about grades and appearances.
  • finances: Stable but closely budgeted household; mother works changing hospital shifts.
  • geography: Pearland, Texas; frequent summer visits to relatives in Louisiana.
  • cultureLanguages: Black American; English at home; church attendance mainly with grandmother during visits.
  • school: Large public high school; biology grades strong, other grades fluctuate with missing work.
  • accessOpportunities: School laboratory classes, phone internet, beauty-store browsing, and occasional library events; after-school transport inconsistent.
  • Age 4–5

    Kayla liked choosing outfits for herself and her sister, though her sister rarely cooperated. She asked her mother why bandages stuck to skin and why scabs changed color. Her mother answered what she could after work. Kayla also enjoyed pretend cooking and long stretches of cartoons, with no particular sign that any one interest would dominate later.

  • Age 6–7

    She liked school when teachers used pictures and demonstrations. Spelling practice bored her, and she negotiated for shorter sessions at the kitchen table. A cousin let her help braid a doll's hair, beginning an interest in styles and products. She sometimes wanted to cut her own hair after a bad day, but her mother insisted they wait until the weekend.

  • Age 8–9

    At nine she received permission to watch selected hair-care videos. She became fascinated by why one product left flakes and another did not. Her experiments were informal mixtures in cups that her mother eventually banned from the bathroom sink. A close friendship ended when the other child moved; Kayla acted indifferent but continued asking relatives whether their family might move back.

  • Age 10–11

    During remote classes Kayla followed beauty creators and fitness accounts with increasing attention. She compared her face with filtered images without always remembering the filters. Her mother criticized the amount of time she spent looking at herself, which made Kayla more secretive. She completed some science activities eagerly and ignored assignments she thought no adult would actually check.

  • Age 12–13

    Puberty made her curious about skin, sweat, and menstrual cycles, partly because classroom explanations seemed too brief. She read product labels and asked a pharmacist a question with her mother nearby. She also believed several confident online claims before a science teacher helped her compare their evidence. She did not become uniformly skeptical; attractive videos still persuaded her quickly.

  • Age 14–15

    Kayla liked biology practicals involving magnification and observable change. She disliked memorizing lists for tests and earned lower marks than she expected. She began posting short hairstyle clips, deleting any that received few reactions. A friendship became strained when a friend posted an unflattering photograph. Her mother dismissed the argument as childish, and they stopped discussing that group in detail.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen she can follow a classroom investigation, record observations, and explain why a comparison needs similar starting conditions. She enjoys the questions more than long reports. She still sometimes stays home after a sleepless night spent messaging and scrolling. Her mother promotes a respected health-related degree; Kayla likes parts of the subject but is uncertain about committing years to it.

Life now

  • enjoys: Questions about skin and bodily changes · Hairstyle videos · Classroom demonstrations · Shopping with her sister
  • avoids: Unflattering group photographs · Long formal reports · Conversations that turn immediately into criticism
  • activities: Occasional hairstyle posts · Biology laboratory classes · Helping sister get ready for school
  • demonstratedSkills: Follows a controlled classroom comparison · Notices differences in texture and appearance · Explains familiar styling steps clearly
  • unfamiliarActivities: Clinical settings · Long independent research projects · Paid customer service · Programming
  • motivations: Feeling attractive and socially included · Understanding changes in her own body · Earning her own spending money
  • ambitions: Interested in further study related to bodies or products · Sometimes imagines building a popular account but has no stable plan
  • struggles: Social-media comparison · Inconsistent sleep and assignment completion · Recurring mother-daughter conflict · Confusing popularity with reliability online
  • supports: Biology teacher welcomes questions · Close sister relationship · Mother provides practical care despite conflict
  • practicalConstraints: Mother’s shift schedule · Limited discretionary money · No regular ride to evening activities

Still uncertain: Which scientific questions sustain her attention away from appearance concerns? · How much does she enjoy making content when reactions are hidden? · Can she and her mother discuss options without treating curiosity as commitment?
